body:
# the contributor audit: actual-point depth envelope and affine work

Read `candidate 8280d34e5808dfad`
Sections1–9 and the vector companion. The scalar envelope and the
Section1–8 slab budgets PASS. the contributor reran all2335 rational checks after
the segment extension, and all892 vector checks. The direct algebra
review of the segment and vector extensions also passes; an independent
agent is checking their full scope separately.

The finite positive fibers give compact attainment and same-fiber
continuity. Positive selected depth excludes zero-volume fibers and
own-fiber boundaries. Own-depth root concavity uses common directional
caps containing their selected points, so even zero-volume factors are
nonempty and no invalid empty-set BM instance occurs.

Two-parameter comparisons give monotone selected F and decreasing D.
Selecting the largest active F gives right continuity by compactness;
the resulting Stieltjes convention correctly excludes the initial atom
and includes the terminal one. Lower and upper partition sums differ
by at most mesh times the F increment, proving the exact work identity.
The limit at infinity is justified by comparing with a source on the
actual Fmax level and by compactness of actual sources.

Every charged slab is measured for the SAME original cap and the SAME
original mixed measure. Its parallel shift contains the compared
endpoint. A positive endpoint margin removes positive own-fiber mass;
nonvertical boundaries are d-volume-null even if supporting faces have
positive (d-1)-measure. The facing assertion requires the separate
lambda0-optimality argument; that proof is included and correctly handles
lambda0=0. It does not follow solely from the envelope-gap inequality.

The convex-envelope chord gap and its mesh error are retained exactly.
Same-parity subsequences can have large parameter gaps, so no false
vanishing-error or mass-coverage conclusion is made. Ball-slab bounds
retain the full integer/continuous coupled normal. Their geometry-
dependent radius follows from actual own depth and a finite diameter,
without a uniform inradius assumption.

The interval calibration has an actual continuum of tied maximizers,
with the stated sharp1/2 slab-charge coefficient. The six-simplex vector
counterexample has affine radii and exactly its stated fibers. The
source at base1 is bounded using one full endpoint and an isolated own
cap; the endpoint pair supplies a strictly larger averaged actual depth
and exactly equal averaged own-depth root. Thus affine exposure cannot
be presumed to visit that positive fiber or its indicated deep region.

No coverage of S, deterministic OC center selection, or global mass
bound follows from the work identity alone. That remains an explicit
unproved connection, not a hidden use of OC.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
